data.description:
# Evaluate whether the munitoai-free rate-limit budget is effective

discovered-from:LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want an evidence-based answer to *"is the
`rate_limit_rpm: 10` budget on the `munitoai-free` tier actually doing its job?"*
— measured from real proxy logs over the first ~12 hours after the budget went
live — so I can keep it, raise it, lower it, or replace it with header-derived
budgeting (`LP-0MVDNP36J006430L`) instead of guessing.

## Context

`LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` shipped in commit `b71d743a` and the proxy was restarted
with it at **2026-10-18 13:59:31 local (BST)**. Live behaviour as designed:

- entries with `rate_limit_rpm` accept at most N dispatches per rolling 60-second
  window (`munitoai-free` is configured with `rate_limit_rpm: 10` on the `plan`,
  `author` and `code` chains — one shared bucket per provider entry name);
- an over-budget request from a **new** session (no affinity) skips the entry
  immediately and the chain continues — it never waits;
- an over-budget request from a session already served by the entry waits (up to
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds`, default 60) for the window to
  drain, then dispatches on the free tier;
- affinity is TTL-scoped (`server.provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`, default 900);
- remaining budget is displayed in the provider diagnostics table on `/`
  (`budget N/10 per 60s`).

The starting value of 10 was a judgement call: the observed peak before the gate
was **41 dispatches per rolling minute** (2026-10-18 11:27) with upstream
`HTTP 429 rate_limit_exceeded` responses at peaks.

## Evaluation method (run against `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`)

Window A (post-change): from the restart marker at `2026-10-18 13:59:31` to the
evaluation time. Window B (baseline, pre-change): the equivalent preceding span
(e.g. 12 h ending 13:59:31) from the same plus rotated logs.

1. **Dispatch rate vs budget** — for every `[remote] POST … ->
   https://api.munito.ai/inference` line, compute the maximum number of
   dispatches in any rolling 60 s window, plus the per-minute distribution
   (median/p95/max) and the count of windows at/over 10. Expect: rolling max
   ≤ 10 (plus in-flight retries of the same logical request, which are not
   separately budgeted).
2. **Skips** — count `Provider budget exhausted:` lines; break down by
   `reason=` (`rate_limited`, `rate_limited_waiters`, `rate_limited_after_wait`,
   `rate_limited_disconnect`) and by `session_affinity=`; confirm every
   `session_affinity=false` skip was followed by a dispatch to the next tier and
   that no wait occurred for it.
3. **Waits** — count `Provider budget wait start|satisfied|exhausted|aborted`
   lines and the distribution of `waited=` values (target ≤ 60 s; flag any wait
   that consumed a large share of a client's latency).
4. **Upstream 429s** — count MunitoAI `429` / `rate_limit_exceeded` occurrences
   in window A vs window B, both absolute and as a share of MunitoAI dispatches.
   Expect a material reduction.
5. **Free-tier utilisation preserved** — share of minutes where the free tier was
   used at all, and mean dispatches per active minute. A budget that is never
   reached means the free tier is under-used (wasted headroom); a budget that is
   always saturated at peak means pressure simply moved to paid tiers.
6. **Regression check** — confirm there is no increase in `All providers
   exhausted` / terminal 503s, and no visible increase in first-token latency on
   the free tier caused by waiting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A reproducible analysis (script or documented commands) is run over the two
   windows and its raw output is attached to this work item as a comment.
2. Measured rolling-60s max dispatches to `munitoai-free` in the post-change
   window is reported against the configured budget of 10, with a verdict on
   whether the gate holds.
3. The skip/waits breakdown (reasons, `session_affinity` split, waited-duration
   distribution) is reported, including explicit confirmation that new-session
   skips did **not** wait and that in-progress waits stayed within the cap.
4. Upstream MunitoAI `429`/`rate_limit_exceeded` rate is compared across the two
   windows (absolute + share of dispatches) and the change is quantified.
5. Free-tier utilisation is reported (share of minutes used, dispatches per
   active minute) with an assessment of over- vs under-restriction.
6. A concrete recommendation is recorded — keep `rate_limit_rpm: 10`, raise it,
   lower it, or hand the value to header-derived budgeting
   (`LP-0MVDNP36J006430L`) — with the evidence that supports it, plus any change
   to `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds` / `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`.
7. If the recommendation changes configuration or code, the change is implemented
   with tests and `proxy/config.yaml` / `proxy/config-fast.yaml` +
   `proxy/README.md` updated; the full project test suite must pass.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect any findings that change
   documented behaviour (code comments, `README`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`).

## Constraints

- Read-only on production state: do not restart the proxy, edit config, or
  change limits as part of the *measurement* (only as a follow-up change per
  AC7, in its own worktree).
- Use the test skill for any test execution; do not run ad-hoc test commands.
- Treat missing log fields as absent, not zero, and state the log window
  boundaries used (rotation can leave gaps).
- Keep the free tier in the chain: the goal is right-sizing, not removal.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` (completed, in_review) — the budget gate this evaluates.
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` (open) — header-derived (`x-ratelimit-*`) budgeting/reset,
  the likely successor for the static value.
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` (open) — restrict the free tier to cheap mode only.
- `LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N` (completed) — per-account 429 must not exclude the paid
  MunitoAI sibling.

## Scheduled dispatch

This item is dispatched automatically **12 hours after the budget went live**
(one-shot cron, 2026-10-19 02:05 local) so a full post-change window exists.
The kickoff script self-removes its cron entry after firing.
data.title: Evaluate whether the munitoai-free rate-limit budget is effective

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Preliminary results — run on demand, 2026-10-18 14:06 (post-change window ≈ 1.05 h)

**Verdict so far: working as designed — keep `rate_limit_rpm: 10` for now; confirm with the full 12 h window at the scheduled 02:05 run.**

**Window correction:** the gate went live earlier than the manual restart I mentioned earlier — commit `b71d743a` landed on `dev` at **12:39:25**, and the api-triggered restart at **13:05:09** loaded it. Post-change window therefore = 13:05:09 → 14:06:19 (1.02 h); baseline = the 12 h ending 13:05:09. Two further restarts fell inside the window (13:25:19 mode→fast, 13:59:38 manual), which reset the in-memory window and interrupted requests.

| Metric | Baseline (12 h) | Post-change (1.02 h) |
|---|---|---|
| `munito.ai` dispatches | 2 846 (3.95/min) | 303 (4.95/min) |
| Rolling-60 s max | **72** @ 01:08 | **11** @ 13:27 |
| Per-minute p50 / p95 / max | 4 / 20 / 44 | 5 / **10** / **10** |
| Minutes at/over the 10 cap | 96 (21.9 % of active min) | 11 (19.3 % of active min) |
| Minutes with any free-tier use | 439 (61.0 % of all min) | 57 (**93.2 %** of all min) |
| Upstream `429` markers | **19** (0.67 % of dispatches) | **0** |
| `All providers exhausted` | 1 | 0 |
| MunitoAI TTFT p50 / p95 | 0.560 s / 19.85 s | 0.587 s / **11.15 s** |

**AC1 — gate holds:** yes. Per-minute dispatch max is exactly 10 and never exceeds it; the single rolling-60 s reading of 11 is edge jitter (the limiter measures at decision time, the log timestamp is the POST a few ms later, so a decision just inside one window can land just outside it).

**AC2 — new sessions pass through with no wait:** 12 `Provider budget exhausted: … reason=rate_limited session_affinity=false` skips, **no wait of any kind** (there is no `session_affinity=false` entry in the wait log), each followed by dispatch on the next tier. Exhaustion diagnostics record them as `status=rate_limited` with `limit_rpm`/`remaining`/`reason`.

**AC3 — in-progress sessions wait, bounded:** 43 `wait start`, **43 satisfied, 0 exhausted, 0 aborted** — every wait produced a free-tier dispatch, none hit the 60 s cap and none lost a client. Wait distribution: p50 **14.1 s**, p95 **52.5 s**, max **55.4 s** (total 843 s across 43 requests, mean 19.6 s). No TTFT regression on the tier (p95 actually improved).

**AC4 — upstream 429s:** 19 in the baseline 12 h → **0** in the post-change hour. This is the failure mode the item was created for: agents were previously burning the allowance into `rate_limit_exceeded`.

**AC5 — free-tier utilisation preserved:** the tier is *not* starved — it is used in 93 % of minutes (vs 61 % baseline) at p50 5 dispatches/min, and saturates the cap in 19 % of active minutes (≈ baseline's 22 %). So the budget is absorbing the burst without idling the free tier.

**AC6 — recommendation:** keep `rate_limit_rpm: 10`; keep `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds: 60` (p95 wait 52.5 s shows the cap is doing real work at the top end — do not raise it without evidence); keep `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds: 900`. Re-check at the scheduled run for: (a) whether the 19 % cap-saturation share rises (would push cost onto paid tiers), (b) whether waits stay under the cap under sustained load, (c) whether upstream 429s stay at zero.

**Caveats:** one hour of data, two in-window restarts, and a 60 s boundary jitter of ±1 dispatch. Figures above are a preliminary read; the one-shot scheduled run at 2026-10-19 02:05 re-measures the full 12 h window and will replace them.

Full python analysis (read-only over `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`): reproduced by the two scripts echoed in `/tmp/budget-eval-report.txt`; method per this item's "Evaluation method" section.
